key: And thou shalt make holy garments for Aaron thy brother, for splendour and for beauty.
s: As Aaron and his sons are called to the priesthood, God turns to their garments; Ramban, on Exodus 28:2, reads it as clothing the priest in royal dignity, since the tunic, mitre, breastplate and plate matched what kings wore when the Torah was given.

evidence.gloss: For splendour and for beauty: that he be honoured and glorified in honoured and glorious garments, as Scripture says, as a bridegroom puts on a priestly diadem (Isaiah 61:10), for these garments are royal garments; kings wore their likeness in the time of the Torah … and the mitre is known even today among kings and great lords … and the ephod and the breastplate are royal dress … and the plate is the crown of kings.

reason: Key verse verbatim (verse.js ok, Exodus 28:2, at [77,2]). Plain sense faithful: 28:1 calls Aaron and his sons to minister in the priest’s office and 28:2 turns to the holy garments (28:4 and 28:40 extend them to the sons). Ramban’s first paragraph on לכבוד ולתפארת says the priest is to be honoured and glorified in garments of royalty, whose likeness kings wore in the time of the Torah, and goes through the chequered tunic, the mitre, the ephod and breastplate, and the plate as royal dress: the sentence carries this without drift. His second reading (על דרך האמת, the honour of the indwelling Name) is a further layer the sentence does not contradict. Rashi has nothing on 28:2; Ibn Ezra and Sforno are briefer.
